rulings.raw: 1 ½ pounds Steaks – excess fat trimmed & cut into generous 1-inch pieces (SEE NOTES)
rulings.evidence: Whole-muscle beef steak cubed for a stir fry: no existing beef id covers it (ground-beef-8020 is a grind, beef-stew-meat is chuck cubes, cube-steak is tenderized round), so a new id is proposed. Sirloin is confirmed by arithmetic, since 201 cal / 20.3 g protein per 100 g raw reproduces the source's published 555 cal and 36 g protein per serving almost exactly; a null here would pantry-price 1 1/2 lb of beef.

rulings.raw: 1 heaping TBS Fresh Thyme Leaves – chopped
rulings.evidence: fresh-thyme is a live board id (4 of 7 per the prior ruling of 2026-08-26), so this is a reuse and not a proposal. Refusing the bridge to dried-thyme: different price class and roughly half the gram weight per spoon.

rulings.raw: 1 tsp EACH: Smoked Paprika & Onion Powder
rulings.evidence: The vocabulary's Onion Powder row is exactly one half of this line; deliberately NOT onions, which is a fresh bulb at a different price and weight. The smoked paprika half cannot get its own ruling because the extraction printed both spices on one raw line, so all 4.7 g is costed as onion powder - stated openly, worth about 1 cal and a couple of cents, and the line should be split upstream.
The cook buys and squeezes a whole fresh lemon, so lemons (5 of 7 stores) is the right commodity; bottled lemon-juice is a different product at a different price class and would misprice the line.
Optional garnish with no stated quantity; named as fresh basil (the lemon wedges come off the lemons already bought). No bid because there is no amount to price, which is pantry-safe.

A three-way serving-base suggestion with no quantity, excluded from the source's own 5 g carb per serving figure; counting any of the three would both invent a quantity and break the run's 35 g carb ceiling.

macro_cross_check.detail: Computed over all 14 lines at the source's own 4-serving scale using the settled grams plus the six I weighed: steak 680 g at 201 cal / 20.3 P per 100 g gives 1368 cal and 138 g protein, and the remaining lines add 845 cal and 6.6 g protein (olive oil 298, butter 402, veg 69, lemon 29, spices and herbs 33, garlic 14). Totals 2213 cal and 144.7 g protein, i.e. 553 cal and 36.2 g protein per serving against the published 555 and 36.0 - a 0.6% protein gap, which is what makes top sirloin (and not ribeye at 240-290 cal/100 g, which would land near 620) the cut this recipe was written for. Carbs compute 8.2 vs the published 5.0 because I count the whole lemon rather than its juice and total rather than net carbs; either figure is far under the 35 g ceiling, and 553 cal sits inside the 400-650 band.
